title: Receipts: what a run leaves behind
summary: Drake never trusts 'it works'; he keeps receipts. A receipt names the commit, the sha256 of the source, compiler and binary, the exact command, the platform, expected next to observed, and the limits of the run. To verify one you rebuild and recompute every field and compare. I can show you a kept receipt for a tiny Omega program, a checker in Omega that compares it field by field, and two negative controls: a one-byte source change (FAIL) and a missing limits line (REFUSED).
goal: Know what a receipt must contain, keep one for an Omega run, and verify it later by recomputing every field.
key_steps: Record commit, source sha256 and compiler sha256
Record the binary sha256 and the exact command
Write expected exit and output before the run, and record observed next to them
Add a limits line saying what the run does not show
Verify by rebuilding, recomputing every field and comparing line by line

example.code:
note rcptchk: check a kept receipt against a fresh recomputation, both read on stdin
note input: the kept receipt, a line "--", then the recomputed receipt; each line is "key value"
note exit 0 PASS, 1 FAIL (a field differs or expected is not observed), 4 REFUSED (shape wrong)
text keys "receipt program omega_mv omc_sha256 source_sha256 binary_sha256 command platform expect_exit observed_exit expect_stdout_sha256 observed_stdout_sha256 limits "
text tsame "fields that match the recomputation: "
text tdiff "DIFF "
text tref "REFUSED "
text tbadk "missing or misplaced key at line "
text tnosep "no -- separator line\n"
text tkept "the kept receipt has "
text tfresh "the recomputed receipt has "
text tneed " lines; a receipt has 13\n"
text texit "kept receipt: expect_exit equals observed_exit: "
text tout "kept receipt: expect_stdout_sha256 equals observed_stdout_sha256: "
text yes "yes\n"
text no "no\n"
text vpass "verdict PASS\n"
text vfail "verdict FAIL\n"
text nl "\n"
const NKEY ulong 13
global lb ulong 64
global lz ulong 64
global nln ulong 1
fn split n ulong to bool
note record the start and end of every line; false when there are more than 64 lines
a = ulong 0
for i ulong n
if eq get inb i 10
c = get nln 0
if ge c 64
ret false
end
put lb c a
put lz c i
put nln 0 add c 1
a = add i 1
end
end
ret true
end
fn issep i ulong to bool
a = get lb i
if ne sub get lz i a 2
ret false
end
if ne get inb a 45
ret false
end
ret eq get inb add a 1 45
end
fn keyok i ulong k ulong to bool
note line i starts with key number k of keys, followed by a space
a = get lb i
e = wordend a get lz i
if eq e get lz i
ret false
end
w = lookup keys a e
ret eq w long k
end
fn lineeq i ulong j ulong to bool
n = sub get lz i get lb i
if ne n sub get lz j get lb j
ret false
end
ret samei get lb i get lb j n
end
fn valeq i ulong j ulong to bool
note the values (after the first space) of lines i and j are equal
a = add wordend get lb i get lz i 1
b = add wordend get lb j get lz j 1
n = sub get lz i a
if ne n sub get lz j b
ret false
end
ret samei a b n
end
fn findsep to ulong
note index of the first "--" line, or the line count when there is none
for i ulong get nln 0
if issep i
ret i
end
end
ret get nln 0
end
fn shape f ulong to bool
note lines f .. f+12 carry the 13 keys in order
for k ulong NKEY
if not keyok add f k k
ot tref
ot tbadk
on add add f k 1
ot nl
ret false
end
end
ret true
end
fn yn b bool to void
if b
ot yes
else
ot no
end
end
fn refuse to int
f = flush
ret 4
end
fn main to int
r = rdall
if lt r 0
ret 4
end
if eq get st 2 1
ret 4
end
if not split ulong r
ret refuse
end
s = findsep
if eq s get nln 0
ot tref
ot tnosep
ret refuse
end
if ne s NKEY
ot tref
ot tkept
on s
ot tneed
ret refuse
end
if ne get nln 0 add mul NKEY 2 1
ot tref
ot tfresh
on sub sub get nln 0 s 1
ot tneed
ret refuse
end
if not shape 0
ret refuse
end
if not shape add s 1
ret refuse
end
bad = ulong 0
for k ulong NKEY
if not lineeq k add add s 1 k
ot tdiff
oi get lb k wordend get lb k get lz k
ot nl
bad = add bad 1
end
end
ot tsame
on sub NKEY bad
ot nl
ex = valeq 8 9
ot texit
yn ex
so = valeq 10 11
ot tout
yn so
if not and ex so
bad = add bad 1
end
if eq bad 0
ot vpass
f = flush
ret 0
end
ot vfail
f = flush
ret 1
end

common_mistake: Keeping a log instead of a receipt, or 'updating' an old receipt after a fix. A receipt is history: keep the old one, add the new one beside it, and add a correction file if the old one was wrong.
